data.title: GPT-5.5 Bank Support Agent Scores Perfectly on Self-Test but Succeeds in Only 5 of 97 Held-Out Cases
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing CryptoSlate, Uniphore researchers found that a GPT-5.5 bank customer service agent earned a perfect score on tests written by its developers but succeeded in only five of 97 held-out cases reviewed by researchers. The agent assumed customers could not be found by name or email, despite those options being available in the simulation. Its own tests instead treated asking customers for an ID as the correct approach, and the agent then rejected other lookup methods.

AppSci-Bench covers seven simulated business workflows, including bank customer service, invoice review, customer relationship management and flight changes. Of 132 builds with recorded self-test results, 86 scored at least 99% on those tests. Across 13 Claude Opus 4.8 builds, iteration raised average self-test scores by 16.9 percentage points and held-out test scores by 3.2 points.

In a separate comparison of 252 builds, the difference in held-out scores between workflows with and without testing and iteration was not statistically significant.

data.title: Goldman Says U.S. Stock Fear Near Historic Extreme, Positioning Flushout Incomplete
data.description:
U.S. stocks have sold off sharply, with the Nasdaq 100 down 19.8% from its record high on October 6, near the bear-market threshold, and the S&P 500 down about 12%; the index fell 8.6% last week, its largest weekly decline in 19 months. The CBOE Volatility Index briefly approached 36, its highest level in 19 months.

According to Odaily, Goldman Sachs’ trading desk said market fear was nearing an extreme, with its volatility fear index reaching 9.8 out of 10 last Friday. Over the past month, systematic strategies such as commodity trading advisers sold about $57 billion in stocks, turning net U.S. equity positioning into a $19 billion short. Hedge funds have cut exposure substantially, but other investors remain heavily invested, and a broad positioning flushout sufficient to support a strong rebound has not occurred.

Goldman said most U.S. CTA selling may be complete and trend-following strategies could become buyers again if stocks rebound. However, risks from potential Federal Reserve rate hikes, uncertainty over returns on AI investment, and market liquidity pressures remain. Goldman said extreme fear does not mean the market has bottomed; tactical buying opportunities may exist, but a sustained rebound would require more positive catalysts.

data.title: Nscale Slows Hiring and Cuts Costs Ahead of Planned $35 Billion IPO
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, British data center operator Nscale is slowing hiring and cutting spending as it prepares for a $35 billion IPO, while streamlining and standardizing its operations. Two people familiar with the matter said Chief Operating Officer Justin Osofsky told employees in an internal email this month that hiring would be paused for the coming months, except for critical roles. The company will also cut nonessential spending. The hiring slowdown does not cover data center construction jobs and mainly affects back-office roles.

Nscale, a startup backed by Nvidia, has Cheryl Sandberg, a former Meta executive, and Nick Clegg, a former UK deputy prime minister, on its board. The company must decide whether to list this year as planned or postpone the IPO until 2027. Its workforce grew from about 300 in early 2026 to about 1,100. Recent declines across AI stocks, investor concerns about debt, and the sudden departure of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang have cast uncertainty over its listing plans. CoreWeave shares fell nearly 30% and Nebius shares nearly 50% over the past month.

This month, Nscale warned it would need additional financing to meet its expected commitments for next year. It estimated revenue of $307 million and a net loss of nearly $1.7 billion for the nine months through September. Two people familiar with its listing plans said Nscale had hoped that Anthropic’s high-profile IPO this week would ease concerns about the AI market and allow it to begin its roadshow within weeks. Anthropic shares, after initially rising above their offering price, fell back to that price during Friday’s broad technology-stock selloff. Nscale has not set a listing timetable, the two people said.

data.title: State Street’s Masahiko Loo Says Treasury-Stock Negative Correlation Has Returned
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Masahiko Loo, chief fixed-income strategist at State Street Investment Management, says US Treasuries are resuming a negative correlation with stocks as US bond futures decline in early Asia trading.

data.title: Michael Saylor: MSTR Earned 34% Annualized Return in Bitcoin Standard Era, Outperforming BTC and Traditional Assets
data.description: Michael Saylor said on X that digital equity is built on digital capital. According to Odaily, MSTR generated an annualized return of 34% during the Bitcoin standard era, outperforming Bitcoin and traditional assets.

data.title: Billionaire Bill Ackman Warns Further Fed Rate Hikes Could Trigger U.S. Recession
data.description:
Billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman warned that further Federal Reserve rate increases could push the U.S. economy into recession. According to Odaily, Ackman wrote on X that the Fed could make another mistake on December 9, as financial conditions have already tightened significantly.

He cited SpaceX, which recently obtained secured debt financing at an 8.259% interest rate, compared with a rate below 6% on unsecured bonds issued at its IPO. Ackman also said the recent sharp decline in stocks had significantly raised the cost of equity financing.

Ackman said a 2% inflation target does not fit the current economic environment. Geopolitical risks, rising global military spending, deglobalization, tariffs, and large-scale investment in AI infrastructure and energy could sustain inflationary pressure, he said. He argued that a 3% inflation target would be more realistic and warned that continued rate increases to bring inflation back to 2% could cause a recession in the U.S. and globally.

data.title: South Korea Exports Rise After Annual Shipments Top $1 Trillion
data.description: South Korea’s exports extended gains in early November, with annual shipments topping $1 trillion for the first time as the global artificial intelligence boom continued to fuel chip demand, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: US Treasury Futures Slip as Stock Futures Advance, Easing Haven Demand
data.description: According to Bloomberg, US Treasury futures declined as demand for haven assets eased after US stock futures advanced.

data.title: CICC: Copper’s Bottom May Be Anchored at $12,500 per Ton
data.description: According to Jin10, a CICC report said copper supply growth from mines is relatively limited and could be revised lower amid various disruptions. AI is expected to provide a considerable boost to demand, while structural inventory tightness caused by U.S. tariffs is likely to persist. Tight supply and demand could drive prices higher. However, slower revenue growth at large-model companies and worsening financing conditions could delay data center construction. If demand temporarily falls short of expectations, copper price volatility could increase; tighter macro liquidity could also weigh on prices, leaving them at risk of a correction in a relatively conservative scenario. Copper prices could be highly volatile over the year, with the bottom potentially anchored at an incentive price of $12,500 per ton and the upper limit at $14,500 per ton. The midpoint is expected to rise further compared with 2026.

data.title: UK Workers Choose Job Security Over Pay in Challenging Labor Market
data.description: British workers are staying in their jobs and accepting stagnant or falling pay in exchange for greater employment security amid the most challenging labor market in recent years, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Libya's NOC: 'Illegal Group' Closes Sharara Pipeline Valve, Expected to Cut Output by 350,000 Barrels a Day
data.description: According to Jin10, Libya's National Oil Corporation said an "illegal group" closed a valve on the Sharara oilfield pipeline, a move expected to reduce daily crude output by about 350,000 barrels.

data.title: STOCKS | South Korea’s KOSPI Opens Down 139.67 Points, or 2.87%, at 4,730.29
data.description: According to Jin10, South Korea’s KOSPI opened 139.67 points lower, down 2.87%, at 4,730.29 on Monday, November 23. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix shares each fell more than 3%.

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | China's Gold Buying Holds $1 Trillion Trade Surplus in Check
data.description: According to Bloomberg, China's gold imports surged to a record $209 billion so far this year in an unprecedented buying spree that followed top officials' promise to make the country the world's marketplace rather than just its factory. The gold buying is keeping China's $1 trillion trade surplus in check.

data.title: Ant Group Leads $100 Million Bet on Simplexity in China’s Humanoid Race
data.description: Chinese physical AI startup Simplexity Robotics received $100 million in a funding round led by Jack Ma-backed Ant Group, according to Bloomberg. Ant Group is betting the startup can compete with more established players in China’s burgeoning robotics arena.

data.title: Korean Memory Chip Stocks Fall Premarket Amid AI Concerns
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Korean memory chip stocks fell in premarket trading as the retreat from the AI trade continued, extending Friday’s sharp U.S. stock sell-off. On the Nextrade platform, Samsung Electronics fell 5.6% and SK Hynix dropped 6%. The declines came despite South Korean authorities’ pledge on Sunday to step up efforts to stabilize the market. On Friday, the S&P 500 entered correction territory, the Nasdaq 100 posted its worst weekly performance since March 2020, and the VIX, known as Wall Street’s fear gauge, surged to its highest level since April 2025. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 5.2% on Friday.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Valuation Shift Puts QDII Fund Net Values Under Pressure
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. stocks sold off sharply in the early hours of November 21 (UTC+8), putting pressure on QDII funds as investors favored companies with nearer-term, more predictable cash flows. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.28% and the S&P 500 dropped 3.70%. Nvidia lost 14.01%, while Bloom Energy fell 15.30% and Lumentum declined 13.94%.

Several fund firms said institutions were repricing long-duration assets, including technology stocks, long-term bonds and copper, as they focused more on current cash flow. They identified Anthropic’s November 19 Nasdaq listing as a potential catalyst. The report said the IPO was priced at $83 per share and raised $107.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX to become the largest IPO globally. Fund managers said the shift toward long-duration pricing also reflected sensitivity to rising long-term U.S. Treasury yields and higher discount rates.

The selloff weighed on QDII returns. Through the evening of November 20, the four worst-performing products for the year were Hong Kong-themed funds, each down more than 38%; the report said such funds commonly held U.S. assets. By contrast, U.S. real estate and consumer-focused QDII funds had held up better over the past month. One QDII investment head said the firm had increased holdings in cash-flow-focused and non-AI technology stocks and had added exposure to Hong Kong companies with high dividends and strong cash flow.

data.title: Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners Agrees to Sell StraitNZ to Partners Group
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Morgan Stanley Investment Management said investment funds managed by Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners have signed an agreement to sell StraitNZ, a New Zealand-based integrated transport, logistics and ferry company, to Partners Group on behalf of its clients. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals and other closing conditions.

data.title: European Natural Gas Prices Extend Gains as Cold Weather Forecast Boosts Sentiment
data.description: According to Sina Finance, European natural gas prices rose sharply in Asian morning trading as the latest weather forecasts turned colder. Dutch TTF front-month natural gas futures climbed as much as 8.6% to 96.075 euros per megawatt-hour. Forecasts show temperatures in northwestern Europe next week are expected to be about 5 degrees Celsius below the 30-year average for the same period.

data.title: STOCKS | Roundhill Strategist Says Selloff May Be Nearing End, but Bulls Still Need Proof
data.description: According to Jin10, U.S. stock index futures rebounded Monday after all three major indexes closed in technical correction territory last Friday. U.S. markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and trading ended early at 1 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time on Friday. Market focus is expected to center on volatile technology stocks as investors assess whether last week's selloff marked a firm market bottom or whether stocks could fall further. Roundhill Chief Investment Strategist Drew Pettit said the broad-based selloff had spread beyond technology, which could be a sign that it was nearing its end. He added that bulls still need to provide sufficient evidence to reverse the pessimism currently dominating the market. Pettit said he believes the market's fundamental bottom is much higher, but that technically, bulls need a series of catalysts to show that the case for long-term earnings growth remains intact.
